behavioral_effects: .gitleaks-baseline.json committed with the three known redacted fingerprints; nightly secret-scan-history runs make secret-scan BASELINE=1 and no longer needs continue-on-error
compatibility_impact: make secret-scan gains an optional BASELINE=1; nightly's full-history job is now gating on anything not in the baseline. .gitleaks-baseline.json is on the read-gate always_allow list.
follow_up: Rotate the three credentials from commit aaec6463 at their providers and then close secrets-pushed-to-remote; the baseline stays as history
reason: The first nightly run failed on the full-history gitleaks scan exactly as predicted: the three findings in commit aaec6463 (backend/.env.example, the open secrets-pushed-to-remote finding) fail any full-history scan, and a nightly that is red every night by design trains people to ignore it. After this change the nightly scan runs against a committed baseline of those three fingerprints (redacted; commit, file, rule and line only), so it fails only on a leak that is not already recorded, while the finding itself stays open until the keys are rotated.
security_impact: The committed .gitleaks-baseline.json holds three fingerprints (commit aaec6463, backend/.env.example, generic-api-key, line) with Secret and Match redacted by gitleaks; no secret value is in the file. The baseline lets the nightly scan detect new leaks against a known past; it does not close secrets-pushed-to-remote, which still needs rotation at the provider. The CI hygiene range scan runs without a baseline.
summary: Give the nightly full-history secret scan a redacted fingerprint baseline so the one known finding does not paint every nightly red

validators_run.evidence_ref: make secret-scan BASELINE=1 over all 123 commits - no leaks found; without the baseline the same scan reports exactly the three recorded fingerprints
make hygiene-workflows clean; pre-commit all-files clean including detect-private-key over the baseline
blocking finding before finish is the absent record; read-surface regenerated for the new root file
